majorat: 1. The right of succession to property according to age; -- so termed in some of the countries of continental Europe. 2. (French Law) Property, landed or funded, so attached to a title of honor as to descend with it.
marionette: 1. A puppet moved by strings, as in a puppet show. 2. (Zoöl.) The buffel duck. MARIOTTE'S LAW Ma`ri*otte's law`. (Physics.) See Boyle's law, under Law.
magniloquence: The quality of being magniloquent; pompous discourse; grandiloquence.
macrozooespore: A large motile spore having four vibratile cilia; -- found in certain green algæ.
maybe: Perhaps; possibly; peradventure. Maybe the amorous count solicits her. Shak. In a liberal and, maybe, somewhat reckless way. Tylor. | Possible; probable, but not sure. Then add those maybe years thou hast to live. Driden.
mammee: A fruit tree of tropical America, belonging to the genus Mammea (M. Americana); also, its fruit. The latter is large, covered with a thick, tough ring, and contains a bright yellow pulp of a pleasant taste and fragrant scent. It is often called mammee apple.
manicheism: The doctrines taught, or system of principles maintained, by the Manichæans.
maleficent: Doing evil to others; harmful; mischievous.
malignify: To make malign or malignant. "A strong faith malignified." Southey.
macrurous: Of or pertaining to the Macrura; having a long tail.
mac: A prefix, in names of Scotch origin, signifying son.
magically: In a magical manner; by magic, or as if by magic.
magdala: Designating an orange-red dyestuff obtained from naphthylamine, and called magdala red, naphthalene red, etc.
maladministration: Bad administration; bad management of any business, especially of public affairs. [Written also maleadministration.]
mascagnin: Native sulphate of ammonia, found in volcanic districts; -- so named from Mascagni, who discovered it.
mauveine: An artificial organic base, obtained by oxidizing a mixture of aniline and toluidine, and valuable for the dyestuffs it forms. [Written also mauvine.]
macrodont: Having large teeth. -- n. A macrodont animal.
marybud: The marigold; a blossom of the marigold. Shak.
magnoliaceous: Pertaining to a natural order (Magnoliaceæ) of trees of which the magnolia, the tulip tree, and the star anise are examples.
magistrally: In a magistral manner. Abp. Bramhall.
marvelousness: The quality or state of being marvelous; wonderfulness; strangeness.
manzanita: A name given to several species of Arctostaphylos, but mostly to A. glauca and A. pungens, shrubs of California, Oregon, etc., with reddish smooth bark, ovate or oval coriaceous evergreen leaves, and bearing clusters of red berries, which are said to be a favorite food of the grizzly bear.
magpie: Any one of numerous species of the genus Pica and related genera, allied to the jays, but having a long graduated tail. Note: The common European magpie (Pica pica, or P. caudata) is a black and white noisy and mischievous bird. It can be taught to speak. The American magpie (P. Hudsonica) is very similar. The yellow-belled magpie (P. Nuttalli) inhabits California.
makeandbreak: Any apparatus for making and breaking an electric circuit; a circuit breaker.
majestatal: Majestic. (old) E. Pocock. Dr. J. Scott.
manganese: An element obtained by reduction of its oxide, as a hard, grayish white metal, fusible with difficulty, but easily oxidized. Its ores occur abundantly in nature as the minerals pyrolusite, manganite, etc. Symbol Mn. Atomic weight 54.8. Note: An alloy of manganese with iron (called ferromanganese) is used to increase the density and hardness of steel.
marmoreal: Pertaining to, or resembling, marble; made of marble.
mastodon: An extinct genus of mammals closely allied to the elephant, but having less complex molar teeth, and often a pair of lower, as well as upper, tusks, which are incisor teeth. The species were mostly larger than elephants, and their romains occur in nearly all parts of the world in deposits ranging from Miocene to late Quaternary time.
maneh: A Hebrew weight for gold or silver, being one hundred shekels of gold and sixty shekels of silver. Ezek. xlv. 12.
mare: The female of the horse and other equine quadrupeds. | Sighing, suffocative panting, intercepted utterance, with a sense of pressure across the chest, occurring during sleep; the incubus; -- obsolete, except in the compound nightmare.
magnesic: Pertaining to, or containing, magnesium; as, magnesic oxide.
mange: The scab or itch in cattle, dogs, and other beasts. Mange insect (Zoöl.), any one of several species of small parasitic mites, which burrow in the skin of cattle. horses, dogs, and other animals, causing the mange. The mange insect of the horse (Psoroptes, or Dermatodectes, equi), and that of cattle (Symbiotes, or Dermatophagys, bovis) are the most important species.
mango: 1. The fruit of the mango tree. It is rather larger than an apple, and of an ovoid shape. Some varieties are fleshy and luscious, and others tough and tasting of turpentine. The green fruit is pickled for market. 2. A green muskmelon stuffed and pickled. Mango bird (Zoöl.), an oriole (Oriolus kundoo), native of India.
mantologist: One who is skilled in mantology; a diviner.
mastigure: Any one of several large spiny-tailed lizards of the genus Uromastix. They inhabit Southern Asia and North Africa.
magaziner: One who edits or writes for a magazine. Goldsmith.
margarine: 1. Artificial butter; oleomargarine. The word margarine shall mean all substances, whether compounds or otherwise, prepared in imitation of butter, and whether mixed with butter or not. Margarine Act, 1887 (50 & 51 Vict. c. 29). 2. Margarin.
mastication: The act or operation of masticating; chewing, as of food. Mastication is a necessary preparation of solid aliment, without which there can be no good digestion. Arbuthnot.
machination: 1. The act of machinating. Shak. 2. That which is devised; a device; a hostile or treacherous scheme; an artful design or plot. Devilish machinations come to naught. Milton. His ingenious machinations had failed. Macaulay.
maintainor: One who, not being interested, maintains a cause depending between others, by furnishing money, etc., to either party. Bouvier. Wharton.
matchmaker: 1. One who makes matches for burning or kinding. 2. One who tries to bring about marriages.
mandil: A loose outer garment worn the 16th and 17th centuries.
malamide: The acid amide derived from malic acid, as a white crystalline substance metameric with asparagine.
manuductor: A conductor; an officer in the ancient church who gave the signal for the choir to sing, and who beat time with the hand, and regulated the music. Moore (Encyc. of Music.)
masterhood: The state of being a master; hence, disposition to command or hector. C. Bronté.
matteroffact: Adhering to facts; not turning aside from absolute realities; not fanciful or imaginative; commonplace; dry.
manucode: Any bird of the genus Manucodia, of Australia and New Guinea. They are related to the bird of paradise.
manred: Homage or service rendered to a superior, as to a lord; vassalage. [Obs. or Scots Law] Jamieson.
macrozoospore: A large motile spore having four vibratile cilia; -- found in certain green algæ.
mainyard: The yard on which the mainsail is extended, supported by the mainmast.
manus: The distal segment of the fore limb, including the carpus and fore foot or hand.
margrave: 1. Originally, a lord or keeper of the borders or marches in Germany. 2. The English equivalent of the German title of nobility, markgraf; a marquis.
makebelieve: A feigning to believe, as in the play of children; a mere pretense; a fiction; an invention. "Childlike make-believe." Tylor. To forswear self-delusion and make-believe. M. Arnold. | Feigned; insincere. "Make-believe reverence." G. Eliot.
maidpale: Pale, like a sick girl. Shak.
macrodiagonal: The longer of two diagonals, as of a rhombic prism. See Crystallization.
marconisystem: A system or wireless telegraphy developed by G. Marconi, an Italian physicist, in which Hertzian waves are used in transmission and a coherer is used as the receiving instrument.
mameluco: A child born of a white father and Indian mother. [S. Amer.]
maltose: A crystalline sugar formed from starch by the action of distance of malt, and the amylolytic ferment of saliva and pancreatic juice. It resembles dextrose, but rotates the plane of polarized light further to the right and possesses a lower cupric oxide reducing power.
mantrap: 1. A trap for catching trespassers. [Eng.] 2. A dangerous place, as an open hatch, into which one may fall.
maistrie: Mastery; superiority; art. See Mastery. (old) Chaucer.
manhood: 1. The state of being man as a human being, or man as distinguished from a child or a woman. 2. Manly quality; courage; bravery; resolution. I am ashamed That thou hast power to shake my manhood thus. Shak.
maxillar: 1. (Anat.) Pertaining to either the upper or the lower jaw, but now usually applied to the upper jaw only. -- n. The principal maxillary bone; the maxilla. 2. (Zoöl.) Of or pertaining to a maxilla.
magniloquent: Speaking pompously; using swelling discourse; bombastic; tumid in style; grandiloquent. -- Mag*nil"o*quent*ly, adv.
massive: 1. Forming, or consisting of, a large mass; compacted; weighty; heavy; massy. "Massive armor." Dr. H. More. 2. (Min.) In mass; not necessarily without a crystalline structure, but having no regular form; as, a mineral occurs massive. Massive rock (Geol.), a compact crystalline rock not distinctly schistone, as granite; also, with some authors, an eruptive rock.
masonry: 1. The art or occupation of a mason. 2. The work or performance of a mason; as, good or bad masonry; skillful masonry. 3. That which is built by a mason; anything constructed of the materials used by masons, such as stone, brick, tiles, or the like. Dry masonry is applied to structures made without mortar. 4. The craft, institution, or mysteries of Freemasons; freemasonry.
marketable: 1. Fit to be offered for sale in a market; such as may be justly and lawfully sold; as, dacayemarketable. 2. Current in market; as, marketable value. 3. Wanted by purchasers; salable; as, furs are not marketable in that country.
marsipobranchia: A class of Vertebrata, lower than fishes, characterized by their purselike gill cavities, cartilaginous skeletons, absence of limbs, and a suckerlike mouth destitute of jaws. It includes the lampreys and hagfishes. See Cyclostoma, and Lamprey. Called also Marsipobranchiata, and Marsipobranchii.
mallet: A small maul with a short handle, -- used esp. for driving a tool, as a chisel or the like; also, a light beetle with a long handle, -- used in playing croquet.
marmoratumopus: A kind of hard finish for plasterwork, made of plaster of Paris and marble dust, and capable of taking a high polish.
magneto: A prefix meaning pertaining to, produced by, or in some way connected with, magnetism.
maziness: The state or quality of being mazy.
magnet: 1. The loadstone; a species of iron ore (the ferrosoferric or magnetic ore, Fe3O4) which has the property of attracting iron and some of its ores, and, when freely suspended, of pointing to the poles; -- called also natural magnet. Dinocrates began to make the arched roof of the temple of Arsinoë all of magnet, or this loadstone. Holland.
magician: One skilled in magic; one who practices the black art; an enchanter; a necromancer; a sorcerer or sorceress; a conjurer.
magnetograph: An automatic instrument for registering, by photography or otherwise, the states and variations of any of the terrestrial magnetic elements.
mara: The principal or ruling evil spirit. E. Arnold. | A female demon who torments people in sleep by crouching on their chests or stomachs, or by causing terrifying visions.
maim: 1. To deprive of the use of a limb, so as to render a person on fighting less able either to defend himself or to annoy his adversary. By the ancient law of England he that maimed any man whereby he… | 1. matelasse: Ornamented by means of an imitation or suggestion of quilting, the surface being marked by depressed lines which form squares or lozenges in relief; as, matelassé silks. | A quilted ornamented dress fabric of silk or silk and wool.
manganesesteel: Cast steel containing a considerable percentage of manganese, which makes it very hard and tough. See Alloy steel, above.
mangostan: A tree of the East Indies of the genus Garcinia (G. Mangostana). The tree grows to the height of eighteen feet, and bears fruit also called mangosteen, of the size of a small apple, the pulp of which is very delicious food.
mackintosh: A waterproof outer garment; -- so called from the name of the inventor.
marker: One who or that which marks. Specifically: (a) One who keeps account of a game played, as of billiards. (b) A counter used in card playing and other games. (c) (Mil.) The soldier who forms the pilot of a wheeling column, or marks the direction of an alignment. (d) An attachment to a sewing machine for marking a line on the fabric by creasing it.
mateology: A vain, unprofitable discourse or inquiry.
maieutic: 1. Serving to assist childbirth. Cudworth. 2. Fig. : Aiding, or tending to, the definition and interpretation of thoughts or language. Payne.
makeup: The way in which the parts of anything are put together; often, the way in which an actor is dressed, painted, etc., in personating a character. The unthinking masses are necessarily teleological in their mental make-up. L. F. Ward.
margosa: A large tree of genus Melia (M. Azadirachta) found in India. Its bark is bitter, and used as a tonic. A valuable oil is expressed from its seeds, and a tenacious gum exudes from its trunk. The M. Azedarach is a much more showy tree, and is cultivated in the Southern United States, where it is known as Pride of India, Pride of China, or bead tree.
martyrologic: Pertaining to martyrology or martyrs; registering, or registered in, a catalogue of martyrs.
mammonite: One devoted to the acquisition of wealth or the service of Mammon. C. Kingsley.
manliness: The quality or state of being manly.
macule: 1. A spot. (old) 2. (Print.) A blur, or an appearance of a double impression, as when the paper slips a little; a mackle. | To blur; especially (Print.), to blur or double an impression from type. See Mackle.
madly: In a mad manner; without reason or understanding; wildly.
manhole: A hole through which a man may descend or creep into a drain, sewer, steam boiler, parts of machinery, etc., for cleaning or repairing.
magged: Worn; fretted; as, a magged brace. Ham. Nav. Encyc.
magnetize: 1. To communicate magnetic properties to; as, to magnetize a needle. 2. To attract as a magnet attracts, or like a magnet; to move; to influence. Fascinated, magnetized, as it were, by his character. Motley. 3. To bring under the influence of animal magnetism.
marver: A stone, or cast-iron plate, or former, on which hot glass is rolled to give it shape.
mammoth: An extinct, hairy, maned elephant (Elephas primigenius), of enormous size, remains of which are found in the northern parts of both continents. The last of the race, in Europe, were coeval with… | Resembling the mammoth in size; very large; gigantic; as, a mammoth ox.
mariet: A kind of bellflower, Companula Trachelium, once called Viola Mariana; but it is not a violet.
maskshell: Any spiral marine shell of the genus Persona, having a curiously twisted aperture.
massy: Compacted into, or consisting of, a mass; having bulk and weight ot substance; ponderous; bulky and heavy; weight; heavy; as, a massy shield; a massy rock. Your swords are now too massy for your strengths, And will not be uplifted. Shak. Yawning rocks in massy fragments fly. Pope.
martin: A perforated stone-faced runner for grinding. | One of several species of swallows, usually having the tail less deeply forked than the tail of the common swallows. [Written also marten.] Note: The American purple martin, or bee martin (Progne…
man: 1. A human being; -- opposed tobeast. These men went about wide, and man found they none, But fair country, and wild beast many [a] one. R. of Glouc. The king is but a man, as I am; | 1. To supply with men; to furnish with a sufficient force or complement of men, as for management, service, defense, or the like; to guard; as, to man a ship, boat, or fort.
macadamization: The process or act of macadamizing.
manatee: Any species of Trichechus, a genus of sirenians; -- called alsosea cow. machiavelism: The supposed principles of Machiavel, or practice in conformity to them; political artifice, intended to favor arbitrary power.
mastodynia: Pain occuring in the mamma or female breast, -- a form of neuralgia.
mandola: An instrument closely resembling the mandolin, but of larger size and tuned lower.
malleate: To hammer; to beat into a plate or leaf.
mantelet: 1. (a) A short cloak formerly worn by knights. (b) A short cloak or mantle worn by women. A mantelet upon his shoulders hanging. Chaucer. 2. (Fort.) A musket-proof shield of rope, wood, or metal, which is sometimes used for the protection of sappers or riflemen while attacking a fortress, or of gunners at embrasures; -- now commonly written mantlet.
marined: Having the lower part of the body like a fish. Crabb.
mansion: 1. A dwelling place, -- whether a part or whole of a house or other shelter. (old) In my Father's house are many mansions. John xiv. 2. These poets near our princes sleep, And in one grave their… | To dwell; to reside. (old) Mede.
marimba: A musical istrument of percussion, consisting of bars yielding musical tones when struck. Knight.
mandolin: A small and beautifully shaped instrument resembling the lute.
mawkish: 1. Apt to cause satiety or loathing; nauseous; disgusting. So sweetly mawkish', and so smoothly dull. Pope. 2. Easily disgusted; squeamish; sentimentally fastidious. J. H. Newman.
mariolater: One who worships the Virgin Mary.
manioc: The tropical plants (Manihot utilissima, and M. Aipi), from which cassava and tapioca are prepared; also, cassava.[Written also mandioc, manihoc, manihot.]
malassimilation: (a) Imperfect digestion of the several leading constituents of the food. (b) An imperfect elaboration by the tissues of the materials brought to them by the blood.
maggoty: 1. Infested with maggots. 2. Full of whims; capricious. Norris.
making: 1. The act of one who makes; workmanship; fabrication; construction; as, this is cloth of your own making; the making of peace or war was in his power. 2. Composition, or structure. 3. a poem.(old) Sir J. Davies. 4. That which establishes or places in a desirable state or condition; the material of which something may be made; as, early misfortune was the making of him. 5.
manifesto: A public declaration, usually of a prince, sovereign, or other person claiming large powers, showing his intentions, or proclaiming his opinions and motives in reference to some act done or contemplated by him; as, a manifesto declaring the purpose of a prince to begin war, and explaining his motives. Bouvier.
manful: Showing manliness, or manly spirit; hence, brave, courageous, resolute, noble. " Manful hardiness." Chaucer. -- Man"ful*ly, adv. -- Man"ful*ness, n.
macaco: Any one of several species of lemurs, as the ruffed lemur (Lemur macaco), and the ring-tailed lemur (L. catta).
marmorean: Pertaining to, or resembling, marble; made of marble.
manumit: To release from slavery; to liberate from personal bondage or servitude; to free, as a slave. "Manumitted slaves." Hume.
marceline: A thin silk fabric used for linings, etc., in ladies' dresses.
marseillais: Of or pertaining to Marseilles, in France, or to its inhabitants. Marseillaise hymn, or The Marseillaise, the national anthem of France, popularly so called. It was composed in 1792, by Rouget de… | A native or inhabitant of Marseilles.
margarous: Margaric; -- formerly designating a supposed acid. (old) MARGARYIZE; MARGARY'S FLUID Mar"ga*ry*ize, v. t. [imp. & p. p. -ized; p. pr. & vb. n. -izing.] [(J. J. Lloyd) Margary, inventor of the process + -ize.] To impregnate (wood) with a preservative solution of copper sulphate (often called Mar"ga*ry's flu"id [-riz]).
mazer: A large drinking bowl; -- originally made of maple. (old) Their brimful mazers to the feasting bring. Drayton.
macroglossia: Enlargement or hypertrophy of the tongue.
marquee: A large field tent; esp., one adapted to the use of an officer of high rank. [Written also markee.]
margaritaceous: Pertaining to, or resembling, pearl; pearly.
mallow: A genus of plants (Malva) having mucilaginous qualities. See Malvaceous. Note: The flowers of the common mallow (M. sylvestris) are used in medicine. mackinaw: A thick blanket formerly in common use in the western part of the United States.
manlike: Like man, or like a man, in form or nature; having the qualities of a man, esp. the nobler qualities; manly. " Gentle, manlike speech." Testament of Love. " A right manlike man." Sir P. Sidney. In glaring Chloe's manlike taste and mien. Shenstone.
malaga: A city and a province of Spain, on the Mediterranean. Hence, Malaga grapes, Malaga raisins, Malaga wines.
macruroid: Like or pertaining to the Macrura.
maikong: A South American wild dog (Canis cancrivorus); the crab-eating dog.
maronite: One of a body of nominal Christians, who speak the Arabic language, and reside on Mount Lebanon and in different parts of Syria. They take their name from one Maron of the 6th century.
mastax: (a) The pharynx of a rotifer. It usually contains four horny pieces. The two central ones form the incus, against which the mallei, or lateral ones, work so as to crush the food. (b) The lore of a bird.
maasha: An East Indian coin, of about one tenth of the weight of a rupee.
marrow: 1. (Anat.) The tissue which fills the cavities of most bones; the medulla. In the larger cavities it is commonly very fatty, but in the smaller cavities it is much less fatty, and red or reddish in… | To fill with, or as with, marrow of fat; to glut.
masting: The act or process of putting a mast or masts into a vessel; also, the scientific principles which determine the position of masts, and the mechanical methods of placing them. Masting house (Naut.), a large building, with suitable mechanism overhanging the water, used for stepping and unstepping the masts of vessels.
makeshift: That with which one makes shift; a temporary expedient. James Mill. I am not a model clergyman, only a decent makeshift. G. Eliot.
madoqua: A small Abyssinian antelope (Neotragus Saltiana), about the size of a hare.
manovery: A contrivance or maneuvering to catch game illegally.
macroprism: A prism of an orthorhombic crystal between the macropinacoid and the unit prism; the corresponding pyramids are called macropyramids.
maudle: To throw onto confusion or disorder; to render maudlin. (old)
marcasitic: Containing, or having the nature of, marcasite.
mammiform: Having the form of a mamma (breast) or mammæ.
malpractice: Evil practice; illegal or immoral conduct; practice contrary to established rules; specifically, the treatment of a case by a surgeon or physician in a manner which is contrary to accepted rules and productive of unfavorable results. [Written also malepractice.]
may: An auxiliary verb qualifyng the meaning of another verb, by expressing: (a) Ability, competency, or possibility; -- now oftener expressed by can. mayoral: The conductir of a mule team; also, a head shepherd.
mahometanize: To convert to the religion of Mohammed; to Mohammedanize.
madreporic: Resembling, or pertaining to, the genus Madrepora. Madreporic plate (Zoöl.), a perforated plate in echinoderms, through which water is admitted to the ambulacral tubes; -- called also madreporic tubercule.
matcher: One who, or that which, matches; a matching machine. See under 3d Match.
markhoor: A large wild goat (Capra megaceros), having huge flattened spiral horns. It inhabits the mountains of Northern India and Cashmere.
magnetomotor: A voltaic series of two or more large plates, producing a great quantity of electricity of low tension, and hence adapted to the exhibition of electro-magnetic phenomena.
martagon: A lily (Lilium Martagon) with purplish red flowers, found in Europe and Asia.
marcasite: A sulphide of iron resembling pyrite or common iron pyrites in composition, but differing in form; white iron pyrites. Golden marcasite, tin. (old)
mancipate: To enslave; to bind; to restrict. (old) Sir M. Hale.
mankind: 1. The human race; man, taken collectively. The proper study of mankind is man. Pore. 2. Men, as distinguished from women; the male portion of human race. Lev. xviii. 22. 3. Human feelings; humanity. | Manlike; not womanly; masculine; bold; cruel. [Obs] Are women grown so mankind Must they be wooing Beau. & Fl. Be not too mankind against your wife. Chapman.
malarial: Of or pertaining, to or infected by, malaria. Malarial fever (Med.), a fever produced by malaria, and characterized by the occurrence of chills, fever, and sweating in distinct paroxysms, At intervals of definite and often uniform duration, in which these symptoms are wholly absent (intermittent fever), or only partially so (remittent fever); fever and ague; chills and fever.
madrigal: 1. A little amorous poem, sometimes called a pastoral poem, containing some tender and delicate, though simple, thought. Whose artful strains have oft delayed The huddling brook to hear his madrigal. Milton. 2.

majordomo: A man who has authority to act, within certain limits, as master of the house; a steward; also, a chief minister or officer.
maniple: 1. A handful. B. Jonson. 2. A division of the Roman army numbering sixty men exclusive of officers, any small body of soldiers; a company. Milton. 3. marchman: A person living in the marches between England and Scotland or Wales.
manumotor: A small wheel carriage, so constructed that a person sitting in it may move it.
maladdress: Bad address; an awkward, tactless, or offensive way of accosting one or talking with one. W. D. Howells.
mannitol: The technical name of mannite. See Mannite.

manitrunk: The anterior segment of the thorax in insects. See Insect.
mammillary: 1. Of or pertaining to the mammilla, or nipple, or to the breast; resembling a mammilla; mammilloid. 2. (Min.) Composed of convex convex concretions, somewhat resembling the breasts in form; studded with small mammiform protuberances.
malacoderm: One of a tribe of beetles (Malacodermata), with a soft and flexible body, as the fireflies.
makingup: 1. The act of bringing spirits to a certain degree of strength, called proof. 2. The act of becoming reconciled or friendly.
marigold: A name for several plants with golden yellow blossoms, especially the Calendula officinalis (see Calendula), and the cultivated species of Tagetes. Note: There are several yellow-flowered plants of different genera bearing this name; as, the African or French marigold of the genus Tagetes, of which several species and many varieties are found in gardens.
maikel: A South American carnivore of the genus Conepatus, allied to the skunk, but larger, and having a longer snout. The tail is not bushy.
malapterurus: A genus of African siluroid fishes, including the electric catfishes. See Electric cat, under Electric.
maidenliness: The quality of being maidenly; the behavior that becomes a maid; modesty; gentleness.

mantle: 1. A loose garment to be worn over other garments; an enveloping robe; a cloak. Hence, figuratively, a covering or concealing envelope. [The] children are clothed with mantles of satin. Bacon. | To cover or envelop, as with a mantle; to cloak; to hide; to disguise. Shak.
mashy: A golf club like the iron, but with a shorter head, slightly more lofted, used chiefly for short approaches. | Produced by crushing or bruising; resembling, or consisting of, a mash.
macaronian: 1. Pertaining to, or like, macaroni (originally a dish of mixed food); hence, mixed; confused; jumbled. 2. Of or pertaining to the burlesque composition called macaronic; as, macaronic poetry.
matrass: A round-bottomed glass flask having a long neck; a bolthead.
maieutics: The art of giving birth (i. e., clearness and conviction) to ideas, which are conceived as struggling for birth. Payne.
maltonic: Of, pertaining to, or derived from, maltose; specif., designating an acid called also gluconic or dextronic acid. See Gluconic.

macedoine: A kind of mixed dish, as of cooked vegetables with white sauce, sweet jelly with whole fruit, etc. Also, fig., a medley.
mayhem: The maiming of a person by depriving him of the use of any of his members which are necessary for defense or protection. See Maim.
marriageability: The quality or state of being marriageable.
marchpane: A kind of sweet bread or biscuit; a cake of pounded almonds and sugar. (old)marzipan Shak.
maharmah: A muslin wrapper for the head and the lower part of the face, worn by Turkish and Armenian women when they go abroad.
manipulate: 1. maigre: Belonging to a fast day or fast; as, a maigre day. Walpole. Maigre food (R. C. Ch.), food allowed to be eaten on fast days.
mall: 1. A large heavy wooden beetle; a mallet for driving anything with force; a maul. Addison. 2. A heavy blow. (old) Spenser. 3. An old game played with malls or mallets and balls. See Pall-mall. | To beat with a mall; to beat with something heavy; to bruise; to maul.
maister: Master. (old) Chaucer. Spenser. | Principal; chief. (old) Chaucer.
maslach: An excitant containing opium, much used by the Turks. Dunglison.
maskery: The dress or disguise of a maske (old) Marston.
maritime: 1. Bordering on, or situated near, the ocean; connected with the sea by site, interest, or power; having shipping and commerce or a navy; as, maritime states. "A maritime town." Addison. 2. manuduction: Guidance by the hand. (old) Glanvill. South.
macco: A gambling game in vogue in the eighteenth century. Thackeray.
mazarine: Of or pertaining to Cardinal Mazarin, prime minister of France, 1643-1661. maniacal: Affected with, or characterized by, madness; maniac. -- Ma*ni"a*cal*ly, adv.
manqueller: A killer of men; a manslayer. (old) Carew.
manoscopy: The science of the determination of the density of vapors and gases.
malting: The process of making, or of becoming malt.
mattoid: A person of congenitally abnormal mind bordering on insanity or degeneracy.
matronage: 1. The state of a matron. 2. The collective body of matrons. Burke. Can a politician slight the feelings and convictions of the whole matronage of his country Hare.
manubial: Belonging to spoils; taken in war. (old) Bailey.
martinetism: The principles or practices of a martinet; rigid adherence to discipline, etc.
maestoso: Majestic or majestically; -- a direction to perform a passage or piece of music in a dignified manner.
macrochires: A division of birds including the swifts and humming birds. So called from the length of the distal part of the wing.
manrent: Homage or service rendered to a superior, as to a lord; vassalage. [Obs. or Scots Law] Jamieson.
manubrium: 1. (Anat.) A handlelike process or part; esp., the anterior segment of the sternum, or presternum, and the handlelike process of the malleus. 2. (Zoöl.) The proboscis of a jellyfish; -- called also hypostoma. See Illust. of Hydromedusa.
malanders: A scurfy eruption in the bend of the knee of the fore leg of a horse. See Sallenders. [Written also mallenders.]
maidenhair: A fern of the genus Adiantum (A. pedatum), having very slender graceful stalks. It is common in the United States, and is sometimes used in medicine. The name is also applied to other species of the same genus, as to the Venus-hair. Maiden grass, the smaller quaking grass. -- Maiden tree. See Ginkgo.
maarashell: A large, pearly, spiral, marine shell (Turbo margaritaceus), from the Pacific Islands. It is used as an ornament.
macedonian: Belonging, or relating, to Macedonia. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Macedonia. | One of a certain religious sect, followers of Macedonius, Bishop of Constantinople, in the fourth century, who held that the Holy Ghost was a creature, like the angels, and a servant of the Father…
maioid: Of or pertaining to the genus Maia, or family Maiadeæ.
manchineel: A euphorbiaceous tree (Hippomane Mancinella) of tropical America, having a poisonous and blistering milky juice, and poisonous acrid fruit somewhat resembling an apple. Bastard manchineel, a tree (Cameraria latifolia) of the East Indies, having similar poisonous properties. Lindley.
marlin: The American great marbled godwit (Limosa fedoa). Applied also to the red-breasted godwit (Limosa hæmatica). Hook-billed marlin, a curlew.
machinate: To plan; to contrive; esp., to form a scheme with the purpose of doing harm; to contrive artfully; to plot. "How long will you machinate!" Sandys. | To contrive, as a plot; to plot; as, to machinate evil.
matureness: The state or quality of being mature; maturity.
malacissation: The act of making soft or supple. (old) Bacon.
macroscopical: Visible to the unassisted eye; -- as opposed to microscopic. -- Mac`ro*scop"ic*al*ly, adv.
maty: A native house servant in India. Balfour (Cyc. of India).
mawk: 1. A maggot. [Scot.] 2. A slattern; a mawks. [Prov. Eng.]
manual: Of or pertaining to the hand; done or made by the hand; as, manual labor; the king's sign manual. "Manual and ocular examination." Tatham. Manual alphabet. See Dactylology. | 1. marquess: A marquis. Lady marquess, a marchioness. (old) Shak.
matchmaking: 1. The act or process of making matches for kindling or burning. 2. The act or process of trying to bring about a marriage for others. | Busy in making or contriving marriages; as, a matchmaking woman.
manoeuvre: 1. Management; dexterous movement; specif., a military or naval evolution, movement, or change of position. 2. Management with address or artful design; adroit proceeding; stratagem. | 1. To perform a movement or movements in military or naval tactics; to make changes in position with reference to getting advantage in attack or defense. 2. To manage with address or art; to scheme.
mastership: 1. The state or office of a master. 2. Mastery; dominion; superior skill; superiority. Where noble youths for mastership should strive. Driden. 3. Chief work; masterpiece. (old) Dryden. 4. An ironical title of respect. How now, seignior Launce ! what news with your mastership Shak.
mar: A small lake. See Mere. [Prov. Eng.] | 1. To make defective; to do injury to, esp. by cutting off or defacing a part; to impair; to disfigure; to deface. I pray you mar no more trees with wiring love songs in their barks. Shak.
maclurea: A genus of spiral gastropod shells, often of large size, characteristic of the lower Silurian rocks.
mad: 1. Disordered in intellect; crazy; insane. I have heard my grandsire say full oft, Extremity of griefs would make men mad. Shak. 2. masterly: 1. Suitable to, or characteristic of, a master; indicating thorough knowledge or superior skill and power; showing a master's hand; as, a masterly design; a masterly performance; a masterly policy. | With the skill of a master. Thou dost speak masterly. Shak.
mastersinger: One of a class of poets which flourished in Nuremberg and some other cities of Germany in the 15th and 16th centuries. They bound themselves to observe certain arbitrary laws of rhythm.
magistracy: 1. The office or dignity of a magistrate. Blackstone. 2. The collective body of magistrates.
malpais: The rough surface of a congealed lava stream. [Southwestern U. S.]
maneuverer: One who maneuvers. This charming widow Beaumont is a nanoeuvrer. We can't well make an English word of it. Miss Edgeworth.
manoeuvrer: One who maneuvers. This charming widow Beaumont is a nanoeuvrer. We can't well make an English word of it. Miss Edgeworth.
marinism: A bombastic literary style marked by the use of metaphors and antitheses characteristic of the Italian poet Giambattista Marini (1569-1625). -- Ma*ri"nist (#), n.
mahabarata: A celebrated epic poem of the Hindoos. It is of great length, and is chiefly devoted to the history of a civil war between two dynasties of ancient India.
malaxator: One who, or that which, malaxates; esp., a machine for grinding, kneading, or stirring into a pasty or doughy mass.
material: 1. Consisting of matter; not spiritual; corporeal; physical; as, material substance or bodies. The material elements of the universe. Whewell. 2. madam: A gentlewoman; -- an appellation or courteous form of address given to a lady, especially an elderly or a married lady; -- much used in the address, at the beginning of a letter, to a woman. The corresponding word in addressing a man is Sir.
marauder: A rover in quest of booty or plunder; a plunderer; one who pillages. De Quincey.
mainmast: The principal mast in a ship or other vessel.
maegbote: Compensation for the injury done by slaying a kinsman. Spelman.
mars: 1. (Rom. Myth.) The god of war and husbandry. 2. (Astron.) maccabean: Of or pertaining to Judas Maccabeus or to the Maccabees; as, the Maccabean princes; Maccabean times.
mammet: An idol; a puppet; a doll. (old) Selden. Shak.
madder: A plant of the Rubia (R. tinctorum). The root is much used in dyeing red, and formerly was used in medicine. It is cultivated in France and Holland. See Rubiaceous. Note: Madder is sometimes used in forming pigments, as lakes, etc., which receive their names from their colors; as. madder yellow. Field madder, an annual European weed (Sherardia arvensis) resembling madder.
mannitan: A white amorphous or crystalline substance obtained by the partial dehydration of mannite.
marguerite: The daisy (Bellis perennis). The name is often applied also to the ox-eye daisy and to the China aster. Longfellow.
magnetomotive: Pertaining to, or designating, a force producing magnetic flux, analogous to electromotive force, and equal to the magnetic flux multiplied by the magnetic reluctance.
massagist: One who practices massage; a masseur or masseuse.
masoolaboat: . A kind of boat used on the coast of Madras, India. The planks are sewed together with strands of coir which cross over a wadding of the same material, so that the shock on taking the beach through surf is much reduced. [Written also masula, masulah, etc.]
macaroni: 1. Long slender tubes made of a paste chiefly of wheat flour, and used as an article of food; Italian or Genoese paste. margent: A margin; border; brink; edge. (old) The beached margent of the sea. Shak. | To enter or note down upon the margin of a page; to margin. (old) Mir. for Mag.
marram: A coarse grass found on sandy beaches (Ammophila arundinacea). See Beach grass, under Beach.

maceration: The act or process of macerating.
macula: 1. A spot, as on the skin, or on the surface of the sun or of some other luminous orb. 2. (Zoöl.) A rather large spot or blotch of color.
mangonel: A military engine formerly used for throwing stones and javelins.
manila: Of or pertaining to Manila or Manilla, the capital of the Philippine Islands; made in, or exported from, that city. malinger: To act the part of a malingerer; to feign illness or inability.
marbrinus: A cloth woven so as to imitate the appearance of marble; -- much used in the 15th and 16th centuries. Beck (Draper's Dict.).

maidenhood: 1. The state of being a maid or a virgin; virginity. Shak. 2. Newness; freshness; uncontaminated state. The maidenhood Of thy fight. Shak.
masterliness: The quality or state of being masterly; ability to control wisely or skillfully.
macramelace: A coarse lace made of twine, used especially in decorating furniture.
manic: Of or pert. to, or characterized by, mania, or excitement.

manorial: Of or pertaining to a manor. " Manorial claims." Paley.
maplike: Having or consisting of lines resembling a map; as, the maplike figures in which certain lichens grow.

malarious: Of or pertaining, to or infected by, malaria. mason: 1. One whose occupation is to build with stone or brick; also, one who prepares stone for building purposes. 2. A member of the fraternity of Freemasons. madrepore: Any coral of the genus Madrepora; formerly, often applied to any stony coral.
mangcorn: A mixture of wheat and rye, or other species of grain. [Prov Eng.]
mameluke: One of a body of mounted soldiers recruited from slaves converted to Mohammedanism, who, during several centuries, had more or less control of the government of Egypt, until exterminated or dispersed by Mehemet Ali in 1811.
manzanilla: A kind of small roundish olive with a small freestone pit, a fine skin, and a peculiar bitterish flavor. Manzanillas are commonly pitted and stuffed with Spanish pimientos.
maxim: 1. An established principle or proposition; a condensed proposition of important practical truth; an axiom of practical wisdom; an adage; a proverb; an aphorism. masculinity: The state or quality of being masculine; masculineness.
mandibular: Of or pertaining to a mandible; like a mandible. -- n. The principal mandibular bone; the mandible. Mandibular arch (Anat.), the most anterior visceral arch, -- that in which the mandible is developed.
majorgeneral: . An officer of the army holding a rank next above that of brigadier general and next below that of lieutenant general, and who usually commands a division or a corps.
maldanian: Any species of marine annelids of the genus Maldane, or family Maldanidæ. They have a slender, round body, and make tubes in the sand or mud.
marechalniel: A kind of large yellow rose. [Written also Marshal Niel.]
martite: Iron sesquioxide in isometric form, probably a pseudomorph after magnetite.
manicate: Covered with hairs or pubescence so platted together and interwoven as to form a mass easily removed.
mahatma: One of a class of sages, or "adepts," reputed to have knowledge and powers of a higher order than those of ordinary men. -- Ma*hat"ma*ism (#), n.
macaw: Any parrot of the genus Sittace, or Macrocercus. About eighteen species are known, all of them American. maingauche: The dagger held in the left hand, while the rapier is held in the right; -- used to parry thrusts of the adversary's rapier.
maxillomandibular: Pertaining to the maxilla and mandible; as, the maxillo- mandibular nerve.
martyrological: Pertaining to martyrology or martyrs; registering, or registered in, a catalogue of martyrs.

manstealer: A person who steals or kidnaps a human being or beings.
malax: To soften by kneading or stirring with some thinner substance.
marmoset: Any one of numerous species of small South American monkeys of the genera Hapale and Midas, family Hapalidæ. They have long soft fur, and a hairy, nonprehensile tail. They are often kept as pets. Called also squirrel monkey.
manumission: The act of manumitting, or of liberating a slave from bondage. "Given to slaves at their manumission." Arbuthnot.
marinade: A brine or pickle containing wine and spices, for enriching the flavor of meat and fish.
magister: Master; sir; -- a title of the Middle Ages, given to a person in authority, or to one having a license from a university to teach philosophy and the liberal arts.
matchless: 1. Having no equal; unequaled. "A matchless queen." Waller. 2. Unlike each other; unequal; unsuited. (old) "Matchless ears." Spenser. -- Match"less*ly, adv. -- Match"less*ness, n.
mayoralty: The office, or the term of office, of a mayor.
maternal: Of or pertaining to a mother; becoming to a mother; motherly; as, maternal love; maternal tenderness. Syn. -- See Motherly.
mandarining: The process of giving an orange color to goods formed of animal tissue, as silk or wool, not by coloring matter, but by producing a certain change in the fiber by the action of dilute nitric acid. Tomlinson.
maistre: Mastery; superiority; art. See Mastery. (old) Chaucer.
malleolar: Of or pertaining to the malleolus; in the region of the malleoli of the ankle joint.

marketer: One who attends a market to buy or sell; one who carries goods to market.
masticin: A white, amorphous, tenacious substance resembling caoutchouc, and obtained as an insoluble residue of mastic.
mandarinism: A government mandarins; character or spirit of the mandarins. F. Lieder.
mauther: A girl; esp., a great, awkward girl; a wench. [Prov. Eng.]
marketing: 1. The act of selling or of purchasing in, or as in, a market. 2. Articles in, or from, a market; supplies.
mass: 1. (R. C. Ch.) The sacrifice in the sacrament of the Eucharist, or the consecration and oblation of the host. 2. (Mus.) The portions of the Mass usually set to music, considered as a musical… | To celebrate Mass. (old) Hooker.
materialist: 1. One who denies the existence of spiritual substances or agents, and maintains that spiritual phenomena, so called, are the result of some peculiar organization of matter. 2. One who holds to the existence of matter, as distinguished from the idealist, who denies it. Berkeley.
maidenhead: 1. The state of being a maiden; maidenhood; virginity. Shak. 2. The state of being unused or uncontaminated; freshness; purity. (old) The maidenhead of their credit. Sir H. Wotton. 3. The hymen, or virginal membrane.
marathi: A Sanskritic language of western India, prob. descended from the Maharastri Prakrit, spoken by the Marathas and neighboring peoples. mazedness: The condition of being mazed; confusion; astonishment. (old) Chaucer.
madrier: A thick plank, used for several mechanical purposes; especially: (a) A plank to receive the mouth of a petard, with which it is applied to anything intended to be broken down. (b) A plank or beam used for supporting the earth in mines or fortifications.
marconi: Designating, or pert. to, Marconi's system of wireless telegraphy; as, Marconi aërial, coherer, station, system, etc.
masoretic: Of or relating to the Masora, or to its authors. Masoretic points and accents, the vowel points and accents of the Hebrew text of the Bible, of which the first mention is in the Masora.
magnetician: One versed in the science of magnetism; a magnetist.
mandibulated: Provided with mandibles adapted for biting, as many insects.
mannitic: Of, pertaining to, resembling, or derived from, mannite. Mannitic acid (Chem.), a white amorphous substance, intermediate between saccharic acid and mannite, and obtained by the partial oxidation of the latter.
magnifico: 1. A grandee or nobleman of Venice; -- so called in courtesy. Shak. 2. A rector of a German university.
